text:
Maya R.: Quick postmortem check-in — last deploy we added a deploy-time seeder that hits a set of top prefixes. After rollout some customers saw latency spikes and the KV cache hit-rate actually dropped for small requests. Any ideas?
Ben K.: saw the same in dashboards, hit-rate for prefix cache dropped from ~72% -> ~48% for 1-32 token requests. latency p95 up ~60ms on those paths.
Carol T.: fwiw the kernel selector change landed in the same PR (switch heuristics for attention kernels). Could be interaction: different batching shapes + warmer traffic = worse KV locality.
Lucas G.: timeline: deploy at 1856012000, seeder cron ran immediately and spawned synthetic bursts to 10k qps for 30s. Autoscaler reacted and added nodes.
Maya R.: that autoscale/hot-add sounds important — newly created workers come up cold (empty KV) and seeder traffic might have been too uniform, not covering the real prefix distribution. result = warmers thrashing cache entries.
Dave H.: also noticed seeder uses simple keying: full prompt hash rather than prefix buckets. so it created lots of distinct keys. believe this raised KV churn.
Ben K.: confirmed. quick grep in logs: seeder id=deploy-seed-2026 generated ~1.3M unique keys in 30s. Our eviction policy couldn't keep up.
Carol T.: suggest two quick mitigations: (1) back off synthetic burst size (2) change seeder to bucket by prefix fingerprint to reduce cardinality.
Maya R.: agree. Proposed policy for next rollout: ramped seeding (10->1000 qps over 10m), prefix-bucket keying, and mark seeder traffic with a header so tracing + cost accounting exclude it.
Lucas G.: +1. Also add a warm-only phase after autoscale: when new node registers, run targeted prefix fill for top-100 prefixes mapped to that capacity zone. avoids global thrash.
infra-bot: deploy "v2.11.4" rolled at 1856012025 by Maya R. (staged).
Dave H.: small sample config for bucketed seeder: 
```
# pseudo config
seeder: 
  mode: prefix-bucket
  buckets: 256
  ramp: { start_qps: 10, end_qps: 1000, duration_s: 600 }
  header: X-Seed-Traffic: true
```

Ben K.: we should add an offline sim to estimate unique key rate given a prefix distribution. i'll run one with prod prompt histogram.
Carol T.: note on kernel selector: we saw that attention kernel A is ~10% faster for >512 seq when batch > 8, but degrades on many small requests — if seeder changes batch shape it can flip selection. consider decoupling kernel selection metric from short-lived seeding traffic by excluding seeded traces from selector telemetry.
Maya R.: action items: Ben run uniqueness sim + produce expected eviction rate, Lucas add warm-only hook for autoscaler flow, Dave update seeder to prefix-bucket mode and ramp, Carol patch kernel selector to ignore seeded header. target: small canary deploy tomorrow AM and gate rollout on hit-rate recovering to >=70%.
Ben K.: I'll post numbers here once sim runs (ETA ~2h).
Lucas G.: I'll stub the autoscaler hook, should be quick.
Dave H.: will cut a small PR for seeder change and add header.
Carol T.: I'll create a telemetry filter for kernel selection and run a backfill so we can compare.
Maya R.: thanks team. also note: keep synthetic -> real traffic ratio low; synthetic should complement, not dominate. :thumbsup:
